hotspotIssueNoCreds: No Wi-Fi hotspot credentials on this device - the hotspot was NOT started. Sync once with internet, or add a network by hand in Settings → Devices → Network.
hotspotIssueRaiseFailed: The Wi-Fi hotspot could not be started: {{message}}
lanSectionHint: Pair devices over your local Wi-Fi to launch games on several screens. Works offline - no internet needed.
rolesExplainIntro: A device can play two distinct, independent roles on the local network:
roleHotspotDesc: The device that creates the Wi-Fi network the others connect to. This is only about connectivity - you can also use an external router instead.
roleMotherDesc: The device that holds the database and where the game is actually launched. Satellite devices connect to it to join the same game.
rolesExplainNote: These roles are independent: the mother doesn't have to be the hotspot. One device can provide the Wi-Fi while another hosts the game, or the same device can do both.
rolesExplainRecommend: That said, we recommend using the same device for both the hotspot and the mother.
sourceHotspotHint: This device creates the Wi-Fi network. Easiest to set up; range is limited by this device's radio and a handful of devices at most.
sourceRouterHint: Ride on a Wi-Fi network from a separate router. Best range and the most simultaneous devices - recommended for larger areas.
routerIntro: Connect this device and every team device to the same router Wi-Fi. The app doesn't join the network for you - pick the router's Wi-Fi in your system settings. Pairing then works exactly like the hotspot.
routerMotherAddress: This device's address on the network: {{addrs}}
routerCredsHint: Optional - only used to show the join QR below. Stored locally, not sent anywhere.
routerQrCaption: Scan to join the router Wi-Fi
routerChecklistIsolation: Turn OFF "AP isolation" / "client isolation" on the router - it blocks devices from seeing each other and breaks pairing.
routerChecklistSameNetwork: Put the mother and every team device on the same network name (not a guest network).
routerChecklistBand: 2.4 GHz reaches further through walls; 5 GHz is faster at shorter range.
noStudioHotspot: No hotspot has been set up for your account yet. It is configured in TagHunter Studio and will appear here after the next sync.
studioManagedHint: Managed in TagHunter Studio. To change the network name or password, contact your administrator.
hotspotBroadcastMismatch: This device is currently broadcasting "{{current}}". The hotspot above was changed in Studio - stop and restart the hotspot (or relaunch the app) to switch to it.
hotspotWindowsOnly: Starting a hotspot from the app is only available on Windows. You can also create one in Windows settings and have devices join it.
firewallHint: If other devices can see this mother but can't connect to it, allow the network port through Windows Firewall. A Windows (UAC) confirmation will appear.
firewallHintChild: If this device can't detect the mother even though it's connected to its Wi-Fi, allow network access (mDNS/UDP) through Windows Firewall. A Windows (UAC) confirmation will appear.
firewallOk: Network access allowed. Devices should be able to connect now.
firewallErr: Couldn't allow access (Windows prompt declined?). Try again and accept the confirmation.
revokeConfirm: Remove this device? It will no longer reconnect on its own: to add it back, use "Join" from that device.
makeMotherConfirm: Hand the game over to this device? It becomes the mother and the other devices reconnect to it.
motherWifiHint: This device must be connected to this network to reach the mother. It joins automatically; scan the code to connect a phone.
noStudioHotspotAdd: No network saved for your account. It's configured in TagHunter Studio and appears after the next sync - or add it by hand below.
addNetworkHint: Saved on this device only. Use it when the mother's Wi-Fi hasn't synced yet. Password: 8 characters minimum.
satelliteHint: Connect to a mother on the same Wi-Fi to receive games launched on it.
discoverEmpty: No mother found nearby. Connect this device to the mother's Wi-Fi, then search again.
troubleshootSameNetwork: Make sure this device is on the same Wi-Fi as the mother (hotspot or router).
troubleshootIsolation: On a router, turn off "AP isolation" / "client isolation" - it hides devices from each other.
troubleshootMotherOpen: Check the mother app is open and set to Host on the same network.
joinAlreadyPaired: This device is already paired with {{label}}. Ask the operator to revoke it there first, then try again.
joinUnreachableFirewall: This device can SEE {{label}} but can't connect to it. This is almost always the MOTHER's firewall: on the mother device, open Settings → Devices → Network and tap “Allow network access” (accept the Windows prompt). If that doesn't help, the mother may have just gone offline.
joinUnreachableSubnet: This device is connected to the Wi-Fi but didn't get a valid address on {{label}}'s network (169.254.x). Open Diagnostics below and tap “Repair IP address (DHCP)” - or, on a router/4G-box venue, put every device on the router's own Wi-Fi.
stepIntro: Connect to the mother in three manual steps. Nothing runs automatically - you start each step and get a detailed message if it fails.
stepSelfHotspotWarn: This device is broadcasting its OWN Wi-Fi hotspot. A child must not host a hotspot on the same 192.168.137.x network as the mother - it breaks this device's address (APIPA 169.254.x) and its route to the mother. Turn off this device's hotspot (Network tab above, or Windows Mobile hotspot) before connecting.
step1Body: Join the mother's Wi-Fi network. The credentials are shown below.
stepNoCreds: No network is configured yet. Add one under “Mother's Wi-Fi” below, or sync once with internet.
stepConnectApipa: Connected to “{{ssid}}” but the hotspot didn't hand out an address (got {{ip}}). Force a fixed IP to reach the mother anyway.
stepForceIpFailed: Couldn't assign a fixed IP (Windows prompt declined?). {{message}}
stepConnectWrongSsid: This device connected to “{{current}}” instead of “{{target}}”. Forget the other network in Windows Wi-Fi settings, or move closer to the mother.
stepConnectNoAssoc: This device didn't connect to “{{ssid}}”. Check the password is correct and that the mother's hotspot is on and in range.
step2Body: Search the Wi-Fi for a running mother.
stepSearchNone: No mother found on this Wi-Fi.
stepSearchNoneHint1: Make sure Step 1 is green (this device is on the mother's Wi-Fi).
stepSearchNoneHint2: Check the mother app is open and set to Host on the same network.
stepSearchNoneHint3: On the mother, allow network access through Windows Firewall (Settings → Devices → Network).
step3Body: Test that this device can actually reach the mother, not just see it.
step3Locked: Find a mother in Step 2 first.
stepPingOk: Reached {{addr}} in {{ms}} ms. This device can connect to the mother.
stepPingFailFirewall: This device sees the mother but the connection is being silently dropped - almost always the MOTHER's firewall. On the mother, open Settings → Devices → Network and tap “Allow network access” (accept the Windows prompt), then retry.
stepPingFailRefused: This device reaches the mother but the connection was actively refused - the mother's game server isn't listening on the hotspot address. On the mother, stop and restart the Wi-Fi hotspot (start the hotspot AFTER the app is open), or restart the app, then retry.
stepPingFailUnreachable: No route to the mother - this device isn't really on the mother's network. Redo Step 1, and if the address stays 169.254.x use “Force a fixed IP”.
stepPingFailGeneric: This device sees the mother but couldn't complete the connection. Retry; if it persists, restart the mother's hotspot and the mother app.
forgetConfirm: Forget this mother? You'll have to pair again.
autoConnectBody: Automatically connect to "{{ssid}}" from now on whenever it's in range?
autoConnectFailed: Couldn't auto-connect to "{{ssid}}" - join the network manually.
rejoinDesc: Look for the device currently hosting and point this one back at it. Use this when this device has lost the game after another device took over as mother. It changes nothing on the mother - try this before taking control.
rejoinDone: Reconnected. The games list and the running game follow the current mother again.
rejoinNotFound: No mother found on the network for this device. Check that both devices are on the same Wi-Fi, then try again.
forceMotherDesc: Make THIS device the mother for the active game. If another device is currently hosting, its latest state is pulled in first so nothing is lost. Use this if this device should be hosting but isn't.
forceMotherDone: This device is now the mother. Open the game to continue - other devices will reconnect.
forceMotherRestarted: This device restarted as the mother for its own game. Other devices will reconnect.
notMotherDesc: Step this device down: it stops hosting games and broadcasting the hotspot, and no longer volunteers as mother at startup. It becomes a satellite and follows the mother on the network.
notMotherActiveGameWarn: This device is currently hosting. Its running games will be unreachable until another device takes control ("Take control as mother" on that device).
notMotherDoneJoined: Done. This device is now a satellite, connected to the mother on this network.
notMotherDone: Done. This device is now a satellite - it will follow a mother as soon as one is available on the network.
connectNotFound: The mother's Wi-Fi isn't in range. Move closer and try again.
connectAlready: Already connected to the mother's Wi-Fi.
diagIntro: Runs a search for mothers and shows this device's mDNS state. Take a screenshot on BOTH the mother and the child.
diagStaticAssigned: Fixed IP address assigned: {{ip}}. Reconnecting to the mother…
diagApipaWarning: This device is connected to Wi-Fi but did not get an address from the mother (169.254.x address). Try "Repair the IP address (DHCP)"; if the address stays 169.254.x, use "Force a fixed IP address" (needs a Windows confirmation) to get a {{range}} address.
diagStaticActive: A fixed IP address is active on this device (used when the hotspot does not hand out an address). DHCP stays on: the internet keeps working normally on other Wi-Fi networks. You can remove it with "Restore DHCP".
diagFirewallMissing: MISSING or outdated (another build of the app) - use "Allow network access" above
relaunchNote: Playground will restart to apply the change.
hotspotBand24: Broadcast the Wi-Fi on the 2.4 GHz band (recommended)
hotspotBand24Hint: Some Wi-Fi cards can't see a 5 GHz access point. Applies the next time the access point starts.
winHealthOk: This mother's Windows settings are fine.
winHealthIssuesTitle: Windows settings to fix on this mother
winHealthHotspotSaving: Mobile hotspot power saving is on: Windows turns the Tag Hunter Wi-Fi off after a few minutes with no device connected.
winHealthSleep: Sleep on mains after {{minutes}} min: the mother would fall asleep mid-game.
winHealthWifiPower: Windows may turn the Wi-Fi card off to save power.
winHealthPublic: Network on the Public profile ({{names}}): satellites may be blocked.
winHealthFixHint: A single Windows permission prompt (UAC) is shown. Hotspot power saving applies the next time the hotspot starts.
mySatellitesHint: The devices connected to this mother.
statusMotherBody: This device is the mother. It broadcasts the {{ssid}} Wi-Fi and {{count}} satellite(s) are connected.
statusMotherRouterBody: This device is the mother, on the {{ssid}} router network. {{count}} satellite(s) are connected.
statusMotherApDownTitle: The Tag Hunter Wi-Fi is not broadcasting
statusMotherApDownBody: This device is the mother, but its access point is stopped: satellites cannot join it.
statusReconnectingBody: This device is reconnecting to the mother on its own. Don't touch anything.
statusSatelliteBody: This device is a satellite, connected to the mother {{mother}} over the {{ssid}} Wi-Fi.
statusLastExchange: Last exchange with the mother {{seconds}} s ago
statusNoMotherOnWifi: This device is a satellite. It is on the {{ssid}} Wi-Fi but can't find a mother.
statusNoMotherNoWifi: This device is a satellite, and it isn't connected to any Wi-Fi.
statusSearchNotFound: Check that the mother is on, that Playground is open on it, and that this device is on the same Wi-Fi.
myMotherNone: This device isn't linked to any mother.
advRoleHintMother: Mother. The role is chosen at installation; only change it if you replace the mother.
advRoleHintSatellite: Satellite. The role is chosen at installation; only change it if you replace the mother.
advModeHint: Mother's Wi-Fi (recommended) or external router, used if this device becomes the mother
advWifiHint: Network name and password, manual entry if not synced
advJoinHint: List the mothers on the network and join one
advWindowsHint: Sleep, hotspot and Wi-Fi card power saving, network profile
advDiagHint: Step-by-step connection, fixed IP address, mDNS search
advRejoinHint: Re-attach to the game's current mother
advResumeHint: If the mother went down: make this device the mother
advNotMotherHint: Step this device down to satellite (not possible while it alone hosts a running game)
